text: Thank you, Chair. So this report is coming back to council for approval. We did have a discussion on the planning position at the council meeting last week on May 17th, with committee approving for us to bring something forward to June 7th. Just based on the current workload and with the resignation that we just received for our receptionist administrative assistant, it is deemed expedient for us to get this job posted. The admin assistant did a lot of the administrative work for the planning side, and we do really need to fill that position seeing that we have that resignation. The job description was reviewed and revised by staff, so the clerk administrator, myself, the CBO, and also another planner looked at the job description. The job description was scored as per our township scoring matrix, with it falling between 29.23 an hour and 35.37 an hour. I know previously this had been brought forward to council, and I believe it fell between $25 and some cents and $26. That was based off 217 wages, because that's when the last review was done. So we took into account COLA, plus we have a 21 point spread between most of our dropped pay grids. So according to our pay review, it would fall between about 53,000 and 64,000 per year based on a 35 hour week or 1,820 hours. So the recommendation is to post for a period of two weeks with the anticipation and hope that we have some good applicants, and start the interview process the week of June 6th to expedite the process, just because we're gonna be slightly short-staffed here in the next little bit. And we have a lot of planning occurring, and we really do need to get someone in that position. In the event that we don't get any applications, we can always extend the deadline further, but we are hopeful that we will get some applications based on the junior planner position, and be able to do that interview process in early June. We would also recommend that council point somebody onto the hiring panel to assist with that, and as far as financial implications, the cost of the position would be covered by the savings in the treasurer position going on to the clerk administrator. So there wouldn't be no negative financial implications on the position being implemented mid-year.
